findings.explanation: encryptCredential() always uses a hard-coded, all-zero 12-byte IV with AES-256-GCM instead of a random nonce. deriveCredentialKey() (line 25) derives the AES key from a single global CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY env var shared by every credential, so every call to encryptCredential() in the process reuses the exact same (key, IV) pair. Reusing a nonce under GCM is catastrophic: it leaks the XOR of any two plaintexts encrypted under the same key/IV and, worse, lets an attacker who sees two such ciphertexts recover the GHASH authentication subkey H and forge valid auth tags for arbitrary ciphertext — fully breaking both confidentiality and integrity of every row in shop_page_credentials.encrypted_value. The fix is to generate a fresh crypto.randomBytes(12) IV per call; the code already threads the IV through the stored envelope (base64UrlEncode(iv) at line 39, base64UrlDecode(ivPart) at decrypt time), so only the IV generation itself needs to change.
